miR‐221/miR‐222 promote growth in H460 but suppress growth in four other NSCLC cell lines through intra‐S phase arrest and/or apoptosis.

miR-221/222 overexpression suppressed the growth of non-small cell lung carcinoma cells through induction of intra-S-phase cell-cycle arrest and/or apoptosis, and that the cells became more sensitive to S-phase-targeting agents.

miR‐221/222 suppresses the growth of non‐small cell lung cancer cells through cell‐cycle arrest and/or apoptosis, and that the microRNAs enhance the efficacy of S‐phase targeting chemotherapeutic drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of miRNA-221 and miRNA-222 on lung cancer cell lines.
the growth‐inhibiting effects of miR221 and miR222 in non-small lung cancer cell lines.
the role of miR‐22 in lung cancer.

the tumor‐suppressive roles of miR-222 are more prominent and consistent than the tumor-promoting roles in non-small cell cancer cell lines.
miR-221/-222 are tumor suppressors in non-small cell NSCLC cells.
miR‐221/222 have both tumor suppressor and tumor promoter roles in non‐small cell lung cancer, and the tumor suppressor roles are more important.

miR‐221/222 has both pro‐ and anti-oncogenic effects in lung cancer, and the effects are cell type specific.
